paper_title: Development and validation of a wearable deep learning continuous in-hospital deterioration prediction model
prediction_task: Binary prediction of in-hospital deterioration (ICU transfer / rapid response / cardiac arrest / in-hospital death) from continuous wearable vitals + EHR, 0.5-24 h horizon, 5 h input window

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Patients selected for wearable patching by nurse clinical judgment with no documented eligibility criteria; strong selection bias risk - nurses chose patients deemed at higher decompensation risk.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added explicit statement that patching was a quality-improvement initiative with nurse-based selection (lines 131-137); acknowledged as limitation for generalization.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Only 11-17 hard deterioration events across cohort insufficient to validate a deep learning predictive model; effectively a feasibility study rather than a validated model.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added Cohen's d-based sample-size justification for wearable-EHR agreement (n=57-74 required); RNN convergence cohort size (888) justified via VC-dimension literature. Acknowledged low event count limitation.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Calibration not assessed; reviewer 3 insisted across 3 rounds that 95%/5% class-rebalancing by over/undersampling distorts probability outputs and demands calibration curves.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added full calibration analyses across 3 validations + recalibration step; transparently reported suboptimal pre-recalibration calibration curves.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Heavy class rebalancing (0.3% -> 5% positive via undersampling+oversampling) on training set risks leakage and skews posterior probabilities in deployment.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Documented resampling approach explicitly; per reviewer demand, added calibration curves demonstrating impact and recalibration correction.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: 'Prospective' validation used same-institution patients on alternate device rather than separate cohort; generalizability across hospitals/populations unassessed.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Clarified retrospective-split nature in abstract; acknowledged device-based rather than cohort-based validation limits generalization claims.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: No TRIPOD/MI-CLAIM compliance; patient-flow diagram absent; discrepancy between 17 deteriorations (Table 1) vs 11 in performance evaluation (Table 3) unexplained.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added MI-CLAIM checklist in resubmission; added Model Training and Testing methods section; agreed to clarify 17 vs 11 patient flow in final revision.
